title: Decode XORed Permutation

monster.name: Decryption Archon
monster.title: Reconstructor of the 1 to N Permutation
monster.defeatQuote: Original permutation of [1, n] decoded from adjacent XOR differences!

description: There is an integer array `perm` that is a permutation of the first `n` positive integers, where `n` is always odd. It was encoded into an array `encoded` of length `n - 1` where `encoded[i] = perm[i] ^ perm[i + 1]`. Given `encoded`, return original `perm`.
solutionCode:
def decode(encoded: list[int]) -> list[int]:
    n = len(encoded) + 1
    total_xor = 0
    for i in range(1, n + 1): total_xor ^= i
    odd_xor = 0
    for i in range(1, len(encoded), 2):
        odd_xor ^= encoded[i]
    perm0 = total_xor ^ odd_xor
    res = [perm0]
    for x in encoded:
        res.append(res[-1] ^ x)
    return res
hints: total_xor is XOR(1..n). XOR of encoded[1], encoded[3], ... gives XOR(perm[1..n-1]). Thus perm[0] = total_xor ^ odd_xor.
